metadata.title: TIMSS 2019 Assessment Frameworks: TIMSS & PIRLS
metadata.venue: TIMSS & PIRLS International Study Center, Lynch School of Education, Boston College; International Association for the Evaluation of Educational Achievement (IEA)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is an assessment framework and does not provide an empirical analysis dataset or an analytic sample. It describes how TIMSS 2019 is organized (fourth and eighth grades; mathematics and science content and cognitive domains) and how questionnaires are developed and used to contextualize learning. Because no student-level estimation results are reported here, the manuscript does not specify whether complex survey weights or replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) are applied, nor does it name any weight variables. For actual TIMSS achievement analyses using the TIMSS international database, analysts should apply the complex survey design weights provided by IEA and use the corresponding replicate weights for variance estimation, consistent with TIMSS data products.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a framework/assessment-design volume that does not estimate models on cognitive achievement outcomes using plausible values (PVs). The text describes content/cognitive domains, questionnaire framework development, and the transition to eTIMSS, but it does not report any PV-based dependent variables or an estimation procedure. Therefore, PV handling and missing-data handling are not applicable to the framework document itself (no empirical modeling is performed).

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No analytic sample is defined because this is an assessment framework document rather than an empirical study. It describes the TIMSS 2019 assessment structure (grades, domains, and questionnaire development) and implementation considerations (eTIMSS and PSI tasks), without reporting student counts or inclusion/exclusion criteria.

data.outcome_summary: TIMSS 2019 Assessment Frameworks documents how TIMSS measures mathematics and science achievement and how it conceptualizes the contexts for learning. The framework is organized by a content dimension (mathematics: Number/Measurement & Geometry/Data at grade 4; Number/Algebra/Geometry/Data & Probability at grade 8; science: Life/Physical/Earth at grade 4; Biology/Chemistry/Physics/Earth at grade 8) and a cognitive dimension (Knowing, Applying, Reasoning) that applies across both subjects and grades. It also outlines the development of the TIMSS context questionnaires through iterative reviews by national research coordinators and an international item review committee. The volume further describes eTIMSS transition plans, including additional problem-solving and inquiry (PSI) tasks and the capability to track students’ problem-solving/inquiry paths via process data. As a framework document, it does not report model performance metrics or achievement benchmarks from an empirical analysis.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is an assessment-framework/report volume rather than an empirical ML paper. As such, it does not define an analytic sample, does not specify PV or missing-data handling for estimation, and does not train or evaluate any machine learning models. Consequently, fields that require empirical outcomes (e.g., main_findings with performance metrics) are intentionally empty.
